summary: This refresh has 650 models, +7 compared with the previous snapshot.
New models include Agnes 3.0 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Reasoning, Max Effort), K2 Horizon 0.9B, K2 Horizon 3.7B, K2 Horizon 7B.
Removed models include GPT-6 Astra (Non-reasoning), Muse Spark 1.3 (max).
Largest metric move: LFM2.5-VL-1.6B on Output speed, from 440.9 tok/s to 0.0 tok/s.
Largest rank move: Nemotron 3 Nano Omni 30B A3B Reasoning dropped 529 places on Output speed.

analysisIdeas.title: Weak-to-strong reachability
analysisIdeas.question: When a source model has lower AA Intelligence Index than a target, can it still reach the target through benchmark wins?

analysisIdeas.title: Benchmark specialization
analysisIdeas.question: Which benchmarks most often let a lower-intelligence model beat a higher-intelligence model?

analysisIdeas.title: Benchmark coverage
analysisIdeas.question: Are some missing chains caused by missing benchmark data rather than poor performance?

analysisIdeas.title: Benchmark correlation
analysisIdeas.question: Which benchmarks track the overall Intelligence Index closely, and which create surprising ranking reversals?

analysisIdeas.title: Bridge models
analysisIdeas.question: Which models most often act as intermediate steps in weak-to-strong chains?

analysisIdeas.title: Provider patterns
analysisIdeas.question: Do some providers produce more specialist models or more bridge models?

analysisIdeas.title: Historical movement
analysisIdeas.question: Do models become better bridges or specialists as benchmarks and model versions change over time?

analysisIdeas.title: Optimization opportunities
analysisIdeas.question: Which benchmark weaknesses should a model improve first to unlock the most new transitive wins?

shortestPathAnalysis.note: Shortest-path metrics are computed from reconstructed shortest paths for each reachable weak-to-strong pair, not by treating reachability alone as a path statistic.
shortestPathAnalysis.interpretation: Many 2-3 hop paths imply a small-world ability graph: models are not linearly ordered, and bridge models connect different benchmark skill islands.

interpretation: Weak models usually beat stronger models by being specialists: they may have a lower AA Intelligence Index but still score higher on one concrete benchmark.
Benchmarks with lower correlation to the Intelligence Index create more surprising wins, because they measure skills that do not move perfectly with the aggregate score.

High-reversal benchmarks are not automatically better or worse. They are useful when they have good coverage and stable margins, because they add information that the aggregate score does not already contain.
Shortest paths are counted from reconstructed shortest paths for each reachable weak-to-strong pair; raw reachability is not treated as a path-length statistic.
Missing benchmark coverage matters. A model with few concrete benchmark values can become hard to connect, even if it has an Intelligence Index.
A practical optimization strategy is to identify benchmarks where a model is below nearby peers, then improve those narrow skills. This can unlock many new direct edges and transitive chains.
